root_cause.text: The ule_mandatory_ext_handlers[] and ule_optional_ext_handlers[] arrays are declared with 255 elements (indices 0-254), but the htype index derived from network-controlled data via (ule_sndu_type & 0x00FF) can reach 255, causing an out-of-bounds array access and potential arbitrary function pointer dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly documents that the arrays have 255 elements (valid indices 0-254) while the bitwise AND operation (ule_sndu_type & 0x00FF) produces a range of 0-255. The fix adds a bounds check `if (htype >= ARRAY_SIZE(ule_mandatory_ext_handlers))` before array access, confirming that index 255 was previously accessible without validation, allowing an OOB read and potential code execution through an unvalidated function pointer call.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability is clearly present in this code. Line 252 derives `htype` from network-controlled data via `p->ule_sndu_type & 0x00FF`, which can produce values 0-255. However, the arrays `ule_mandatory_ext_handlers` and `ule_optional_ext_handlers` are declared with only 255 elements (lines 244 and 248), meaning valid indices are 0-254. When `htype` equals 255, the array accesses at lines 257 and 273 will read out-of-bounds memory. Line 257 accesses `ule_mandatory_ext_handlers[htype]` and line 258 dereferences it as a function pointer, and similarly line 273 accesses `ule_optional_ext_handlers[htype]` and line 274 dereferences it. There is no bounds checking to prevent `htype` from reaching 255, making this a classic out-of-bounds array access vulnerability with potential arbitrary function pointer dereference.
